reviewBinding.applicability: This verdict applies only to the two exact byte strings above. The author was concurrently hardening the candidate; any changed candidate or checker requires a new review.
reviewBinding.reasonNotFrozenByteReview: This was an adversarial pre-freeze audit requested while the author was still working. It is a durable rejection of the reviewed bytes, not acceptance or rejection of a later successor.

reviewed: crash, retry, response-loss and partial-publication behavior
old capability rejection across fresh sessions
D9 failure derivation and pre-commit RunId visibility
same-content Run convergence across distinct Attempts
notClaimed: integration into claim-register, threat model, completeness or narrative authorities

method.probeExecution: Targeted Python probes imported the reviewed checker with python3 -B and manipulated only its executable design-test-double state. No repository fixture or candidate byte was changed.
method.decisionRule: A green authored checker is checker-scope evidence only. The review required the executable transition to falsify the binding's declared invariants and separately mutated the binding to test whether the checker consumed those declarations.
method.normalFixtureResultUse: The existing green normal/selftest result was not treated as acceptance. Decisive counterexamples exercised states and contract mutations outside its authored scenario set.

blockingFindings.finding: The executable cannot commit a second distinct Attempt whose semantic inputs produce an already committed Run. It treats the four exact pre-existing Run-scoped peers as a forbidden partial final set, contradicting the binding's convergence rule.

setup: Under the same project/store, cold-resolve the same EAS and prepare the byte-identical semantic bundle for exec1-audit-converge-b.
Invoke commit_run for the second Attempt.
probe.observed: LedgerCorrupt: partial or conflicting final record set

blockingFindings.consequence: Content-derived Run identity cannot converge across correlation-distinct Attempts as designed; an implementer must invent whether exact shared peers are valid or corrupt.
requiredRepair: Classify the four exact Run-scoped peers as valid shared preexistence when all four are present and byte-identical.
Atomically add the second Attempt's exact AttemptRunLinkV1 and outbox rows and remove only its journal.
Continue to reject incomplete or conflicting shared peers and one-sided Attempt-specific peers.
Add sequential and interleaved two-Attempt convergence probes.

blockingFindings.finding: _rehydrate validates exact Attempt and journal state before _commit_rehydrated, but the modeled transaction later checks only that a journal key exists. It does not condition the swap on the exact Attempt revision or journal bytes it validated.

probes.mutationBetweenRehydrateAndCommit: increment frozen Attempt revision from 1 to 2
probes.observed: all six records committed; stored Attempt revision remained 2

probes.mutationBetweenRehydrateAndCommit: replace journal.semanticEvidenceCasRef with sha256: followed by 64 f characters while preserving the closed journal shape
probes.observed: all six records committed and the changed journal was deleted

blockingFindings.consequence: The checker does not implement the binding's in-transaction reread/conditional-write rule and can finalize stale preparation authority.
requiredRepair: Carry an exact journal and Attempt revision snapshot or commitment into finalization.
Inside the modeled transaction, require exact equality with that snapshot before writing or deleting anything.
Model a conditional compare-and-swap or serializable predicate that prevents a concurrent state change from being lost.
Add Attempt, journal, private material and custody changes between rehydrate and commit as adversarial probes.

blockingFindings.finding: recover_run returns NoPreparedRun whenever both AttemptRunLinkV1 and the journal are absent, without detecting other final peers. This contradicts the unconditional declaration that any partial six-record set is LEDGER.CORRUPT.

setup: Insert its exact RunIndexV1 as the sole final record.
Remove the preparation journal and invoke recover_run by ExecutionId.
probe.observedException: NoPreparedRun: no journal or committed Attempt link

blockingFindings.consequence: Recovery cannot meet its advertised partial-state totality. Some RunId-keyed orphan peers cannot be attributed from ExecutionId without an additional completeness/index authority.
requiredRepair: Add an execution-scoped completeness authority sufficient to detect all six peers, or assign RunId-keyed orphan detection to an explicit ledger-wide integrity API.
Narrow the recovery claim if detection is intentionally impossible from ExecutionId alone.
Test every one-through-five peer subset both with and without a journal.

blockingFindings.finding: Trusted EP8/RT13/store corruption may escape as raw ValueError, but d9_for_failure handles only Evidence LedgerCorrupt and CommitFailed. The declared persisted-hash/index mismatch to LEDGER.CORRUPT mapping is therefore not total.

probe.setup: After preparation, delete the EvaluationAuthorityAdmission CAS row named by the durable authority index, then invoke recover_run and map its failure through d9_for_failure.
probe.recoveryObserved: ValueError: authority admission CAS row missing or ambiguous
probe.d9Observed: TypeError: failure has no Evidence v7 D9 mapping

blockingFindings.consequence: A specified durable corruption path has no HostTermination derivation and can bypass the D9/RunId visibility contract.
requiredRepair: Classify trusted durable-store, EP8 and RT13 reconstruction failures at the E7 boundary without converting caller/programmer errors into ledger faults.
Mechanically derive the class/code from the pinned D9 authority rather than literals.
Add missing, duplicate, wrong-kind, cross-project, noncanonical and index-drift D9 probes.

blockingFindings.finding: prepare_run_commit blindly replaces the durable custody row set at a content-derived preparationRef. Unlike private CAS, Attempt and journal writes, it does not enforce absent-or-exact equality.

setup: Prepare once and retain its custodyPreparationRef.
Change one stored custody row's recordCasRef under that same key.
probe.observed: The conflicting durable row set was overwritten with the producer-derived rows and preparation succeeded.
probe.expected: LEDGER.CORRUPT with the conflicting stored state unchanged

blockingFindings.consequence: A producer retry can silently repair or erase evidence of durable custody corruption, so row presence is not trustworthy recovery authority.
requiredRepair: Publish custody rows insert-or-exact as one closed set.
Reject missing, extra, duplicate or differing pre-existing rows under the same preparationRef.
Add exact retry and corruption-preservation probes.

blockingFindings.finding: Cold-image restore validates final records only as dictionaries before deriving keys. It does not enforce exact fields, schema version, ref/RunId syntax, constants or row ProjectId equality for any of the six final record kinds.

probe.setup: Append a RunIndexV1 carrying projectId prj1_evil and an unknown field to an otherwise valid durable image, then restore it.
probe.observed: Restore accepted the row into the project state's RunIndexV1 map under key (prj1_evil, run1:aaaa...).
probe.expected: Closed-boundary rejection before the row enters durable state

blockingFindings.consequence: Cold restart admits cross-project and open-schema durable rows, breaking project isolation and hostile-ledger totality.
requiredRepair: Define and execute exact validators for TerminalRunV1, RunIndexV1, AttemptRunLinkV1, CustodyRootV1, RunAuthorityIndexV1 and outbox.
Apply them on restore, trusted read and write, including project equality and content/hash relationships.
Reject wrong container types even when empty and test unknown, null, scalar, duplicate and cross-project cases.

blockingFindings.finding: The checker admits the new root records but validates selected names, lengths and substrings rather than their closed obligations. In particular, recoveryMatrixContract is never semantically consumed by check().
blockingFindings.consequence: The artifact can contradict the executable oracle and protected identity boundary while remaining green; the producer's declaration is acting as its own oracle.
requiredRepair: Close and exact-check the entire E7 successor delta or provide a schema with additionalProperties false and semantic cross-field checks.
Mechanically equate requiredScenarios with the executable matrix scenario set.
Mutation-test every authority, identity-exclusion, recovery-order, precondition and failure-visibility obligation.
Treat mutation failure-to-apply as an escape.

blockingFindings.finding: The binding exposes two names for the same custody-root record and two generations for its consumed authority contracts. The closed record schema/persisted list uses RunCustodyRootV1, while FINAL_WRITES, finalTransaction and executable code use CustodyRootV1. Protected surfaces still name EP7, RT12 and VERSIONING v7 while dependencies and execution consume EP8, RT13 and VERSIONING v8.

probe.method: Cross-field and checker-source comparison of exact strings
observed: RunCustodyRootV1 in the declared records/persisted list
CustodyRootV1 in the executable six-write set
EP7/RT12/VERSIONING-v7 in semanticJoins and persisted/correlation text
EP8/RT13/VERSIONING-v8 in dependencies, invariants and executable imports

blockingFindings.consequence: A greenfield implementer must invent an alias and decide which provider generation is normative, creating the week-one fork the freeze process is intended to prevent.
requiredRepair: Choose one canonical custody-root record name and use it in schemas, APIs, transactions and checkers.
Update consumed-generation labels or declare an exact, machine-checked compatibility projection from EP8/RT13/V8 to preserved predecessor identities.
Do not preserve stale prose merely to retain predecessor artifact bytes when the successor artifact itself is not a semantic identity.

residualFindings.finding: E7 mints and cold-remints PreparedCustodyV1 from an exact list of CustodyPreparedObjectV1 rows but does not execute or explicitly import RT13 resolve-and-pin, availability, lease or fencing authority. The EP8 durable fixture contains five authority/semantic CAS rows while the RT13 closure names 23 proof objects; most referenced raw objects are absent from every modeled E7 durable object map, yet finalization succeeds.
residualFindings.requiredDisposition: Either integrate a guarded RT13 prepared/pinned capability whose authority is cold-restorable and validates object existence plus exact pins, or state and mechanically verify that CustodyPreparedObjectV1 rows are store-authoritative pin records with transactional existence constraints. Binding/ref presence alone must not confer custody.

residualFindings.finding: d9_for_failure hard-codes operational-failed, LEDGER.CORRUPT and DURABILITY.COMMIT_FAILED. The checker hash-pins D9 files but does not import the declared reference derivation or recompute these values from D9 axes/code maps.
residualFindings.requiredDisposition: Load and validate the pinned D9 authority, construct the exact fault axes, call the reference derivation, and assert class, ordered code payload and exit-code consequence.

residualFindings.finding: neither-index-nor-link and both-exact are hard-coded alias rows. The underlying happy-path behavior is exercised elsewhere, but _matrix_errors does not validate either row's content. Partial rows likewise do not assert their exact publicCounts.
residualFindings.requiredDisposition: Execute each named scenario directly or mechanically construct the alias from an executed result, validate every field, and add contract mutations for scenario removal and semantic reversal.

scopedPositiveObservations: The normal fresh-session path reconstructs EP8 authority from durable CAS/index rather than a candidate cache.
The reviewed matrix rejects old EP8 handles and old finalized/custody capabilities when presented to a fresh session.
The modeled six-write happy path uses copy/validate/swap and response-loss retry verifies an exact committed set.
Prepared journal records omit direct RunId, runSealRef and Terminal refs.
These observations are strictly narrower than, and do not offset, the blocking counterexamples.

checkerScopeBoundary.decisiveEvidence: Each rejection is based on a concrete transition counterexample, an escaping contract mutation, or a direct contradiction between binding surfaces; no finding depends only on a nonzero checker exit.

authorityBoundary.statement: This artifact records a rejection of exact pre-freeze bytes. It does not apply patches, accept CD-RT-5, close V10/G19/R2-FINAL-03, promote EVIDENCE or OPERABILITY, or authorize architecture freeze.

finalDisposition.nextGate: Repair every blocking finding, adjudicate the custody-authority join, close the checker/D9/matrix residuals, freeze new exact hashes, rerun the full packet, and obtain a new independent frozen-byte review.
